title: Pulled Pork Mac and Cheese
seoTitle: Pulled Pork Mac and Cheese | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: BBQ meets mac — hall legend
description: BBQ meets mac — hall legend. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Rub and slow-cook pork
steps.instruction: Coat pork shoulder with brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Slow-roast covered at 275°F or slow-cooker on low 8 hours until shreddable at 203°F.

steps.title: Shred and sauce pork
steps.instruction: Rest pork 20 minutes, then shred. Toss with vinegar and BBQ sauce — pulled pork mac needs actual pulled pork, not marinara chicken pasta.

steps.title: Make mac and cheese
steps.instruction: Boil macaroni al dente. Make cheese sauce with butter, flour, milk, cheddar, and Monterey Jack. Fold pasta into sauce.

steps.title: Combine and pan up
steps.instruction: Fold shredded BBQ pork into mac and cheese. Transfer to buttered hotel pans; top with optional panko.

steps.title: Bake until bubbling
steps.instruction: Bake at 375°F 20–25 minutes until edges bubble and top browns. Hold at 200°F for the line.

steps.title: Serve for a big crew feed
steps.instruction: Scoop hearty portions — protein and mac in every serving. Extra BBQ sauce on the side for crews who want more smoke.

proTips: Firefighters eat heavy after rough nights — double the protein if the hall had a busy shift.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Pulled Pork Mac and Cheese with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Serve family-style from two full-size trays — never let the line run dry on a busy night.
Put starch and protein on separate trays so vegetarians can load up on sides.
Line up Pulled Pork Mac and Cheese on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: BBQ meets mac — hall legend. A hall pick for big-appetite nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Any short pasta shape works — penne, rigatoni, or spaghetti.
